title: Instagram’s Data Download Dilemma: A Deep Dive into Data Portability and Privacy
summary: Instagram's data download feature allows users to export their personal data, such as photos, comments, and activity. This tool not only provides transparency and empowerment aligned with GDPR privacy laws but also sparks a surge in third‑party content downloaders and privacy debates. Dive into how this feature is shaping user behavior, addressing recent security breaches, and impacting the data portability landscape.
body_markdown:
In January 2026, Instagram faced a significant data breach that exposed the personal information of approximately 17.3 to 17.5 million users. The breach, allegedly carried out by a hacker using the alias "Solonnik," led to the leaking of user names, email addresses, phone numbers, and partial location data on the dark web. Notably, passwords were not compromised in this incident. Link Insertion Paragraph If your personal information was exposed in a breach, discovering a[phone number found on dark web](https://coveron.com/blog/phone-number-found-on-dark-web/) can be an important warning sign that your contact details may have been compromised and could require additional security measures.


Meta, Instagram's parent company, traced the breach back to a vulnerability in the application's API that had existed since 2024, prompting a wave of password reset emails to affected users. The incident has spurred increased reliance on Instagram's official data export tools for users to verify and secure their personal information, aligning with ongoing privacy concerns and the importance of data portability[as discussed in cybersecurity reports](https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/heres-the-truth-about-instagram-data-breach-2026/) .
